newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Johnnic launches share sales scheme.
newsitem.headline: Johnnic launches share sales scheme.

text.p: South Africa's Johnnies Industrial Corporation (Johnnic) chairman Cyril Ramaphosa on Thursday launched a suspensive share sales scheme of 9.1 million shares in the firm and said the scheme would further black economic empowerment.

The Ikageng scheme sets aside 6.4 million Johnnic shares, or six percent of Johnnic, to smaller members of the National Empowerment Consortium which bought a controlling 35 percent stake in Johnnic from Anglo American Corporation of South Africa Ltd in October last year.
A further 2.7 million shares, or 1.8 percent of Johnnic, will be offered to blacks, coloureds and Asians only.
"It is important for the social and economic stability of our country that people on the ground should benefit directly from the economic changes taking place," Ramaphosa said at the launch.

The scheme will open on April 22 and close on June 6. Investors will subscribe for a minimum of 50 shares at 66 rand each and put down a deposit of six rand per share. The balance would be payable on May 31, 2000.

Investors in the scheme will not have voting rights and will not receive dividends, but will enjoy the benefits of a rise in the share price at the end of the period. The shares may also not be traded or ceded during the three year period.
A trust has been set up to administer the shares and vote on behalf of investors and will be disolved at the end of three years.
